sections.heading: Glamsterdam Devnet 7 Status
sections.summary: Devnet 7 is stable; transaction load increased for further analysis, with builder bid and performance issues under investigation.
sections.body:
- Network held up well over the weekend; transaction load has been ramped up with different scenarios for a 24-hour stress test round.
- Geth builder has gas limit issues and is not winning any bids; Nethermind builder is also not winning bids — both under investigation.
- TISM (adversarial/chaos) scenarios started by Pari, including ePBS mutator flipping bits in bids and planned targeted PTC vote drops.
- Stefan testing a builder scenario to win slot 31 (epoch transition) and withhold the block, but clients are self-building instead of accepting higher bids.
  - Request for CL clients to review bid acceptance logic and add logging when bids are rejected.
  - Pari asked for circuit breaker logging; Lodestar confirmed a warning log: "Builder circuit breaker activated, ignoring builder bids".
  - Teku identified as favoring local blocks ~90% of the time; Teku merging bid reprocessing improvements with added debug logging.
  - Prysm logs every ignored bid.
- Besu rolled back a performance improvement that introduced a state handling regression; fix in progress.
  - Per chat: the reverted changes should be the last ones needed; bugs introduced by the improvements need fixing before re-merging.
- Performance report linked: [self-built blocks analysis](https://panda-uploads-production.devops-539.workers.dev/panda/uploads/20bd08/glamsterdam-devnet-7-self-built-blocks.html).

sections.heading: Benchmarking and Client Optimization Status
sections.summary: Most EL clients have optimizations merged on devnet 7; repricing benchmarks started but final numbers unlikely before next week.
sections.body:
- Maria asked each EL client whether optimizations are already pushed to devnet 7 to interpret benchmark results correctly.
- Reth: everything should be there.
- Nethermind: all merged, including EL-CL change support.
- ethrex: will add optimizations to devnet 7 today.
- Erigon: most optimizations present but performance regressions noticed; needs updated benchmark instructions (Jochem to share after call).
- Geth: everything on master branch except parallel execution, which will be merged today or tomorrow.
- Repricing analysis started Friday on devnet 7; Luis working on a benchmark suite release.
  - Final repricing numbers unlikely by next Wednesday; possibly available sometime next week.
  - Devnet 7 results expected to be sufficient for locking final numbers; devnet 8 would serve as confirmation.
- Toni noted that final repricing numbers also affect one or two BAL-related tests/constants that still need updating and testing.

sections.heading: Devnet 8 Planning and Timeline
sections.summary: Devnet 8 launch date deferred to next ACDT; pending repricing numbers, spec releases, and CL alpha.13.
sections.body:
- Devnet 8 spec sheet shared: [glamsterdam-devnet-8 notes](https://notes.ethereum.org/@ethpandaops/glamsterdam-devnet-8).
- Devnet 8 should be as similar as possible to devnet 7, with targeted additions.
- Key changes for devnet 8:
  - discv5-only on the EL side (no discv4 fallback); clients asked to confirm they can surface errors rather than silently falling back.
  - SSZ fork transition testing prioritized — this was a pain point on devnet 7.
  - More chaos/adversarial testing planned; devnet 7 preserved for app developer use.
- Stefan suggested next Wednesday as launch target; Maria and Mario flagged this as too tight given pending repricing numbers and spec releases.
- CL specs team planning an alpha.13 release for devnet 8 by end of this week, hopefully mid-week.
- Barnabas questioned whether devnet 8 changes could just be rolled into devnet 7; Pari argued at least one more devnet with a smooth fork transition is needed.
  - potuz confirmed a consensus-breaking attestation tracking fix that requires a new devnet.
- Decision: revisit devnet 8 launch date at next ACDT call.
- Reth asked whether devnet 8 is the last devnet and whether testnet/mainnet timelines should be discussed; Mario noted CL teams are needed for that discussion.
  - Pari has previously advocated for a devnet 9 focused on chaos/adversarial testing.

sections.heading: EIP-8070 Sparse Blob Pool Engine API for Devnet 8
sections.summary: Agreement to include EIP-8070 Engine API changes (GetBlobsV4, FCU custody_columns) in devnet 8; cell-level DAS deferred.
sections.body:
- Bosul (networking team) proposed making [EIP-8070](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/2170#issuecomment-5091899084) Engine API changes mandatory for devnet 8, while deferring the cell exchange (req/resp 72) part.
  - Two components: Engine API changes (GetBlobsV3/V4, FCU with custody_columns field) and actual cell-level DAS.
  - Having both GetBlobsV3 and V4 available lets clients use whichever is more efficient for their current implementation.
  - FCU with custody_columns field enables EL-side sparse blob pool simulation.
- Hive tests for the Engine API changes are almost ready; Spencer confirmed EELS engine API tests exist, with Geth and Nethermind passing.
- EL client readiness:
  - Geth: proposal originates from Geth team; strongly supportive.
  - Nethermind: good, has PR; already running sparse blob pool on devnet 7.
  - Reth: already merged on main.
  - Besu: fine to implement Engine API part.
  - Erigon: not a priority but fine if just Engine API changes.
  - ethrex: no problem.
- CL client readiness:
  - Lighthouse: PRs ready to go.
  - Lodestar: Engine endpoints are straightforward.
  - Nimbus (Dustin): needs at least one or two CLs to drive testing; not strongly opposed.
- Debate on custody_columns in FCU:
  - Daniel Knopik (Lighthouse) raised concern about embedding custody_columns in FCU rather than a separate RPC method, noting Lighthouse internal pushback.
  - potuz agreed it feels wrong to keep overloading FCU.
  - Bosul explained rationale: avoids adding a new Engine API method; custody_columns is one field, called every slot if changed; avoids separate failure handling.
  - Currently on devnet 7: FCU V4 with custody_columns as optional parameter (Geth implementation); Lighthouse not yet sending it.
  - Daniel Knopik noted compatibility is fine if all clients treat the parameter as optional.
- Agreement: Engine API changes are a go for devnet 8; any implementation concerns to be raised async and revisited next ACDT.
- [Execution APIs PR 774](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/774) linked for the sparse blob pool Engine API spec.

sections.heading: EIP-2780 Log Cost Simplification
sections.summary: No objections to merging EIP-2780 changes for devnet 8; only create transactions see pricing changes.
sections.body:
- [EIP PR 11997](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/11997) — already merged at the EIP level.
- Maria explained: removes the special call-out of log transfer cost for ether transfer events, simplifying the EIP without changing pricing in most cases.
  - Exception: create transactions do see a pricing change.
- [EELS PR 3214](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/pull/3214) (Guru) and [EELS PR 3238](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/pull/3238) (Spencer) already in progress for spec updates.
- No objections from EL clients; confirmed for inclusion in devnet 8.

sections.heading: EIP-8037 Renaming Regular Gas to Execution Gas
sections.summary: Consensus to rename 'regular gas' to 'execution gas' for forward compatibility; no behavioral or consensus changes.
sections.body:
- [EIP PR 11998](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/11998) — already merged.
- Proposed by Jochem; renames "regular gas" to "execution gas" to be forward-compatible with potential future gas dimension splits.
- Luis (Besu) raised that execution gas currently also covers networking-related costs (call data, blobs); Maria and Jochem explained this is intentional for forward compatibility — call data costs are intrinsic gas and may be separated in a future fork.
- Jochem emphasized that the EIP document is what the community reads and cannot be changed after the fork, making correct naming important now.
- draganrakita (Reth) and Luis (Besu) both agreed the new name is an improvement over "regular gas."
- No objections; spec updates already done by Spencer.

sections.heading: EIP-7997 Factory Contract at Fork Boundary
sections.summary: Both open PRs to be closed; the EIP text already correctly states clients must not check for the contract at the fork boundary.
sections.body:
- Two open PRs discussed: [EIP PR 11991](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/11991) (Toni) and [EIP PR 12009](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12009) (Jochem).
- Issue: on chains where the EIP-7997 factory contract is not yet deployed at Glamsterdam activation, should the contract address appear in the block access list (BAL) / execution witness?
  - On mainnet this is a no-op — the factory is already deployed.
  - Only affects hypothetical other chains activating Glamsterdam without prior factory deployment.
- Current client behavior: no client reads the factory account at the fork boundary except Geth, which has an `Apply7997`-style check.
  - This means Geth would diverge from other clients on a chain where the factory is missing — but this is irrelevant for mainnet.
- Jochem read the current EIP text aloud: "Client software MUST NOT check for the existence of the contract at the fork boundary" — this already captures the desired behavior.
- Kevaundray (zkVM perspective) confirmed this is fine; guest programs will hard-code the contract.
- Agreement: close both PRs, keep the EIP as-is.
  - Geth may optionally simplify their code to remove the fork-boundary check, aligning with all other clients.
  - Marius (Geth): not married to their current behavior, willing to align.
- Testing: no need to add tests for the factory-not-deployed case since it cannot occur on mainnet and is out of the EIP's scope.
